correctness.rationale: The proof characterizes maximality by unmatched cross-shore pairs. In the unbalanced case, any matching smaller than m leaves one smaller-shore vertex and at least two larger-shore vertices unmatched, forcing an extendable edge. In the balanced case, maximal matchings have size at least n-1. One or two deletions leave an explicit prescribed edge that cannot participate in any size-(n-1) maximal matching; with at least three deletions, a deleted index disjoint from the prescribed edge can be left unmatched and Hall's theorem supplies the residual perfect matching. All boundaries 2<=m<=n and 0<=t<=m are covered. Exhaustive enumeration through n=6 independently reproduces every local minimum and the global formula; the finite check is not used as the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper defines the same invariant and settles only the undeleted complete-bipartite boundary in this family. Its full text has no matching/crown treatment in the relevant section. Classical edge domination optimizes the size of one smallest maximal matching and does not imply the maximum over prescribed-edge minima; the balanced one- and two-deletion cases demonstrate the separation. Targeted semantic searches and prior-record comparison found no statement covering the matching-deletion threshold.
residual_risks: Because the invariant was only recently named, older matching-theory work may contain an equivalent prescribed-edge statement under different terminology.
The classical edge-domination source was used for its standard global-minimum relation, not for a whole-document claim of noncoverage.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a full natural perturbation profile for a recently introduced edge invariant. It identifies a sharp third-deletion transition in the balanced canonical family and proves that every strict imbalance removes the transition. It also isolates a meaningful difference between ordinary edge domination and prescribed-edge dom-saturation, rather than merely recomputing a known minimum matching parameter.
